# #4427: Patch: on a short phone held upright, End turn and your hand stay on the screen
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
On a small phone held upright, such as an iPhone SE in Safari with its address bar showing, the game board is taller than the screen. The cards stop shrinking at their smallest size. The bottom of the board, which holds your hand and the End turn button, is cut off below the edge of the screen, where it cannot be scrolled to. Once this is built, a short phone gets a fit of its own, as a phone on its side already does. Your hand shows the top part of each card (its cost, name and first line), a tap lifts a card to read it, and End turn stays on the screen. Taller phones see no change.

## Why
- The upright phone board sizes every card from the board's own height: `--card-h: clamp(44px, calc((100cqh - 330px) / 5.24), 94px)` (`apps/web/src/game/board.css:3410`). The cards stop at 44px, so a board under about 330 + 5.24 × 44 ≈ 561px tall needs more room than it has. With a rail (an online match's Back row, `--board-rail-phone-h: 62px`, `board.css:3562-3564`) it needs about 623px.
- The stylesheet already says the cards are at that 44px floor at 390×664 (`board.css:4180-4182`, B46). A 375×548 screen (an iPhone SE in Safari with its bars showing) is 116px shorter than that.
- Both hosts clip what does not fit. The practice shell is exactly the visible viewport tall, with `overflow: hidden` (`apps/web/src/practice/practice.css:1433-1439`). A match's host is a `100dvh` grid (`board.css:4110-4118`). The board's last rows are the ones lost: your hand, and the control bar that holds End turn.
- Phone landscape already solved this with a peek of your hand (`board.css:3912-3931`, `:4046`). A phone held upright has no short-height rule. `apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts` names only `short: 500` (a phone on its side), and no `@media` in `board.css` reads a portrait height.
- No test looks. The smallest upright size in `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx` (`VIEWPORTS`, line 13) is 390×664, where `#2876 End turn and your hand stay on screen at 390x664` runs (line 1156). `mobile-ux.cy.tsx`'s `BAR_VIEWPORTS` (line 993) does include 320×568 and 375×667. But `expectOneRow` (line 1041) checks only that the bar's buttons share one row inside the screen's width, never its height.
- The overflow figures above are worked out from the stylesheet, not measured in a browser. Step 1 below measures them.

## Proposal
1. Add the failing rows first. Run the `#2876` End-turn-and-hand test and the no-overflow describe in `board-layout.cy.tsx` at 375×548 and 320×568 upright, and at about 360×560 (a small Android phone with Chrome's bars), with and without a rail. Record on `main` how far End turn's bottom edge lands below the screen.
2. Name a short-portrait breakpoint in `breakpoints.ts`: a phone held upright whose window is at most about 620px tall. The build picks the exact height from step 1's measurements, and `breakpoints.test.ts` holds every sheet's `@media` to the named breakpoints.
3. Under that breakpoint, the upright board gives back height as the landscape layout does:
   - Your hand's row becomes a peek. The top of each card shows, a tap lifts the card clear to read it, and a drag starts from the part that shows.
   - The card budget's 1.24 share for the hand drops to the peek's share, so the four field rows keep their 44px floor.
   - Only if that is still not enough, the seats' plates compact.
   - Taller phones keep today's layout exactly.
4. The Duos board keeps its own budget (`apps/web/src/duos/duos.css:589-593`) and is left alone. The PR says whether it needs the same rule, as a follow-up.

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts`, `apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts` (the new name)
- `apps/web/src/game/board.css`: one short-portrait block beside the `max-width: 600px` one
- `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`: the new sizes
- `apps/web/README.md`, where it describes the phone layouts
- SPEC: none. This is layout only; no rule changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `board-layout.cy.tsx` runs `#2876 End turn and your hand stay on screen` at 375×548, 320×568 and 360×560, with and without a rail, and the PR shows it failing on `main` with the measured overflow.
- [ ] At those sizes, End turn's bottom edge and every hand card's visible part are inside the screen, nothing scrolls either way, and every field card is at least 44px tall.
- [ ] A peeking hand card lifts clear on a tap and can be dragged from the part that shows (component test).
- [ ] At 390×664, 390×844 and the other existing `VIEWPORTS`, every existing layout test passes unchanged, including `#2876 your hand keeps its size at 390x844` and `#2932`'s area check.
- [ ] `breakpoints.test.ts` passes with the new named breakpoint.

## Size and risks
Medium: about 4-6 files, one CSS block of roughly 40-80 lines, and the spec rows.
- The upright phone board's CSS carries many earlier fixes (#2876, #2932, #3633's single layout pass). The new block should override only custom properties and the hand row, never re-lay the field.
- On those phones a hand reads as a peek, not as whole cards. That is the trade phone landscape already makes.
- Cypress component runs are slow, so add rows only where they prove something.

## Goal
On a short phone held upright (such as an iPhone SE at 375×548 in Safari, 320×568, and 360×560), the upright board keeps the End turn button and your hand within the screen with zero horizontal or vertical scroll overflow, while preserving at least a 44px height floor for every field card. Hand cards in upright short-portrait mode display as a peek showing cost, name, and first line of text; tapping a card lifts it clear of the fan and seat to be fully read, and dragging initiates normally from the exposed portion. Taller portrait phones (e.g. 390×664, 390×844) and other layouts are untouched and continue to pass all existing layout tests.

- [`apps/web/src/game/cardSizes.test.ts`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/apps/web/src/game/cardSizes.test.ts):
  - Test `#3341 board.css declares each layout's --card-h from BOARD_CARD_BUDGET`: asserts `board.css` declares `shortPortrait`'s `--card-h` budget matching `BOARD_CARD_BUDGET`.
  - Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test apps/web/src/game/cardSizes.test.ts`
- [`e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx):

- [ ] `board-layout.cy.tsx` measures and documents on `main` the overflow at 375×548, 320×568, and 360×560 with and without rail.
- [ ] `shortPortrait: 620` is added to `BREAKPOINT_PX` and `AXIS` in [`apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts).
- [ ] `apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts` passes with the new named breakpoint.
- [ ] `BOARD_CARD_BUDGET` in [`apps/web/src/game/config.ts`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/apps/web/src/game/config.ts) and [`apps/web/src/game/cardSizes.test.ts`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/apps/web/src/game/cardSizes.test.ts) updated for `shortPortrait`.
- [ ] `@media (max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)` added to [`apps/web/src/game/board.css`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/apps/web/src/game/board.css) implementing the peek and adjusted card budget.
- [ ] At 375×548, 320×568, and 360×560 (with and without rail), End turn bottom is on screen, document does not scroll either way, and every field card is at least 44px tall.
- [ ] A peeking hand card lifts clear on tap and can be dragged from the visible portion (proved in Cypress component test).
- [ ] Existing viewports (390×664, 390×844, desktop, landscape, tablet) pass all layout tests unchanged.
- [ ] [`apps/web/README.md`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4427/apps/web/README.md) documents `shortPortrait` and the upright phone peek layout.
- [ ] Harness checks pass: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Risks
- **Breaking taller portrait phones**: If the media query or CSS specificity bleeds into 390×664 or 390×844, hand sizes or field areas on standard phones could regress. *Mitigation*: The media query strictly requires `(max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)`, which excludes 664px and 844px. Verified by existing `#2876 your hand keeps its size at 390x844` and `#2932` area check.
- **Field cards dipping below the 44px floor**: If budget subtraction is too small or denominator is miscalculated, field cards could shrink under 44px. *Mitigation*: The budget recalculation explicitly guarantees `--card-h >= 44px`, and the test directly checks `card.height >= 44 - SLACK_PX`.
- **Click/Drag target obstruction**: In peek mode, if the hand slot clips pointer events or overlapping z-index from the control bar interferes with hand cards or vice versa. *Mitigation*: Component test specifically clicks and drags from the exposed top strip of a hand card, confirming interaction functions cleanly.
- **Duos layout impact**: Duos has a separate rail height and budget (`duos.css:591-593`). *Mitigation*: Duos is left untouched as required; the PR note will mention Duos follow-up.

## Open questions
None. All requirements, viewports, and mechanisms are well-defined by the issue and existing landscape peek precedent.

# Plan: #4427 Patch: on a short phone held upright, End turn and your hand stay on the screen

## Goal
On a small phone held upright (such as an iPhone SE at 375×548 in Safari, 320×568, and 360×560), the upright board keeps the End turn button and your hand within the screen with zero horizontal or vertical overflow, while maintaining at least a 44px height floor for every field card. Hand cards in upright short-portrait mode display as a peek showing cost, name, and first text line; tapping a card lifts it clear of the fan and seat to be fully read, and dragging initiates normally from the exposed portion. Taller portrait phones (e.g., 390×664, 390×844) and other layouts are untouched and continue to pass all existing layout tests.

## Files to touch
| File | Action | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts` | change | Add `shortPortrait: 620` to `BREAKPOINT_PX` and `"height"` to `AXIS`, with docstring explaining the upright short phone breakpoint. |
| `apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts` | change | Update `#3227` breakpoint count assertion from 5 to 6, asserting `BREAKPOINT_PX`, `upTo("shortPortrait")` = `(max-height: 620px)`, and `over("shortPortrait")` = `(min-height: 621px)`. |
| `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | change | Add `@media (max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)` block: adjust `--card-h` budget denominator and fixed deductions (hand peek share ~0.52 to 0.6 instead of 1.24), set `.board > .hand-you` height to peek height (`calc(var(--hand-card-h) * 0.52 + 8px); align-items: flex-start;`), lift transform `translateY` offset to rise clear above seat, and compact seats/padding if needed. |
| `apps/web/README.md` | change | Update the breakpoint list to include `shortPortrait 620 px` and document the short-portrait peek behavior under phone layouts. |
| `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx` | change | Add short-portrait viewports (375×548, 320×568, 360×560 with and without rail) to the `#2876` End turn and hand check, verifying End turn and hand cards are inside viewport without overflow and field cards are >= 44px; add component test verifying a peeking hand card lifts on tap and is draggable from the visible part. |

Files / crates / apps MUST NOT touch:
- `crates/*`, `apps/admin/*`, `apps/edge/*`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md`, `.github/*`, `.harness/*`, `.squishy/*`, `bot/*`, `apps/web/src/duos/duos.css`.

Spec sections and rulings:
- None (layout and client presentation only; does not affect engine rules).

## Steps
1. **Baseline reproduction & measurements in `board-layout.cy.tsx`**:
   - In `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`, add a temporary runner or run `#2876` at 375×548, 320×568, and 360×560, with and without a rail.
   - Record the exact baseline overflow values on `main` (how many pixels End turn's bottom edge sits below the viewport height) to include in the PR description.
2. **Define `shortPortrait` breakpoint in `apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts`**:
   - In `BREAKPOINT_PX`, add:
     ```ts
     /** A phone held upright on a short screen: End turn and hand peek (#4427). */
     shortPortrait: 620,
     ```
   - In `AXIS`, add `shortPortrait: "height"`.
3. **Update named breakpoint assertions in `apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts`**:
   - In `#3227 names five breakpoints...`, update to expect six breakpoints (`phone: 600, narrow: 760, medium: 899, tablet: 1024, short: 500, shortPortrait: 620`).
   - Add assertions for `upTo("shortPortrait")` (`(max-height: 620px)`) and `over("shortPortrait")` (`(min-height: 621px)`).
   - Verify `pnpm --dir apps/web test apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts` passes.
4. **Implement short-portrait layout in `apps/web/src/game/board.css`**:
   - Directly adjacent to `@media (max-width: 600px)`, add `@media (max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)`.
   - In `.board`:
     - Reduce the hand budget share in the denominator:
       `--card-h: clamp(44px, calc((100cqh - 330px) / 4.52), 94px);`
       and with rail:
       `--card-h: clamp(44px, calc((100cqh - 330px - var(--board-rail-phone-h)) / 4.52), 94px);`
       (Where 4.52 represents 4 field rows + 0.52 peek share).
     - If the 330px fixed deduction is too large on 548px/560px viewports with a rail, compact the seat padding/tray channels (e.g., `--tray-channel: 14px`, reduce seat vertical padding) within this media query so that `--card-h` remains at least 44px.
   - In `.board > .hand-you`:
     - Set height to peek: `height: calc(var(--hand-card-h) * 0.52 + 8px); align-items: flex-start;`
     - `.board > .hand-you .hand-cards { align-items: flex-start; }`
   - In `.hand-you .hand-slot[data-lifted="true"]`:
     - Ensure lifted cards transform upwards clear of the fan and seat:
       `transform: translateY(calc(var(--hand-card-h) * -0.5 - 8px)) scale(var(--hand-lift-scale));`
       `transform-origin: calc((var(--i, 0) + 0.5) / var(--n, 1) * 100%) 100%;`
     - Played card: `transform: translateY(calc(var(--hand-card-h) * -0.5 - 8px));`
5. **Update documentation in `apps/web/README.md`**:
   - In "The breakpoints are one named set", add `shortPortrait 620 px (a phone held upright on a short screen)`.
   - In the phone layout description, document the short-portrait peek behavior and tap-to-lift mechanism.
6. **Add layout and interaction tests in `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`**:
   - Extend `#2876 End turn and your hand stay on screen` (or add `#4427 End turn and your hand stay on screen on short phones upright`) for viewports `375×548`, `320×568`, and `360×560`, both with and without a rail:
     - Assert `endTurn.getBoundingClientRect().bottom <= height + SLACK_PX`.
     - Assert hand cards' visible portions are on screen.
     - Assert `doc.documentElement.scrollHeight <= height` and `doc.documentElement.scrollWidth <= width`.
     - Assert all 20 field cards have `box.height >= 44 - SLACK_PX`.
   - Add a component test for tap-to-lift and drag on a peeking card at 375×548:
     - Click the exposed top of a hand card (e.g. `[data-testid^="hand-card-"]`).
     - Assert the card slot gains `data-lifted="true"`.
     - Assert the lifted card bounding box is visible, scaled up, and within screen bounds.
     - Trigger pointerdown and move on the visible top of the card; assert drag to play initiates (`document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-dragging") === "play"`).
7. **Regression testing**:
   - Verify that at 390×664, 390×844 and other `VIEWPORTS`, every existing layout test passes unchanged (including `#2876 your hand keeps its size at 390x844` and `#2932`).
   - Run vitest tests and harness checks.

## Tests
- `apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts`:
  - Test `#3227 names six breakpoints, each a max N beside a min N + 1`: asserts `BREAKPOINT_PX.shortPortrait === 620`, `upTo("shortPortrait") === "(max-height: 620px)"`, `over("shortPortrait") === "(min-height: 621px)"`.
  - Test `#3227 every @media width and height in src/'s stylesheets is a named breakpoint or KEEP's`: asserts `board.css` uses only named breakpoints.
  - Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts`
- `e2e/cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`:
  - Test `#2876 End turn and your hand stay on screen at 390x664, 375x548, 320x568 and 360x560, with and without a rail`: asserts End turn bottom <= height + slack, hand visible inside screen, no scroll overflow, and field cards >= 44px.
  - Test `#4427 a peeking hand card lifts clear on a tap and can be dragged from the part that shows at 375x548`: asserts card lifts on tap with `data-lifted="true"` and initiates play drag on pointer movement.
  - Command: `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --spec cypress/component/board-layout.cy.tsx`

## Done when
- [ ] `board-layout.cy.tsx` measures and documents on `main` the overflow at 375×548, 320×568, and 360×560 with and without rail.
- [ ] `shortPortrait: 620` is added to `BREAKPOINT_PX` and `AXIS` in `apps/web/src/breakpoints.ts`.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/breakpoints.test.ts` passes with the new named breakpoint.
- [ ] `@media (max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)` added to `apps/web/src/game/board.css` implementing the peek and adjusted card budget.
- [ ] At 375×548, 320×568, and 360×560 (with and without rail), End turn bottom is on screen, document does not scroll either way, and every field card is at least 44px tall.
- [ ] A peeking hand card lifts clear on tap and can be dragged from the visible portion (proved in Cypress component test).
- [ ] Existing viewports (390×664, 390×844, desktop, landscape, tablet) pass all layout tests unchanged.
- [ ] `apps/web/README.md` documents `shortPortrait` and the upright phone peek layout.
- [ ] Harness checks pass: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Risks
- **Breaking taller portrait phones**: If the media query or CSS specificity bleeds into 390×664 or 390×844, hand sizes or field areas on standard phones could regress. *Mitigation*: The media query strictly requires `(max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)`, which excludes 664px and 844px. Verified by existing `#2876 your hand keeps its size at 390x844` and `#2932` area check.
- **Field cards dipping below the 44px floor**: If budget subtraction is too small or denominator is miscalculated, field cards could shrink under 44px. *Mitigation*: The budget recalculation explicitly guarantees `--card-h >= 44px`, and the test directly checks `card.height >= 44 - SLACK_PX`.
- **Click/Drag target obstruction**: In peek mode, if the hand slot clips pointer events or overlapping z-index from the control bar interferes with hand cards or vice versa. *Mitigation*: Component test specifically clicks and drags from the exposed top strip of a hand card, confirming interaction functions cleanly.
- **Duos layout impact**: Duos has a separate rail height and budget (`duos.css:591-593`). *Mitigation*: Duos is left untouched as required; the PR note will mention Duos follow-up.

## Open questions
None. All requirements, viewports, and mechanisms are well-defined by the issue and existing landscape peek precedent.

## Risks
- **Breaking taller portrait phones**: If the media query or CSS specificity bleeds into 390×664 or 390×844, hand sizes or field areas on standard phones could regress. *Mitigation*: The media query strictly requires `(max-width: 600px) and (max-height: 620px)`, which excludes 664px and 844px. Verified by existing `#2876 your hand keeps its size at 390x844` and `#2932` area check.
- **Field cards dipping below the 44px floor**: If budget subtraction is too small or denominator is miscalculated, field cards could shrink under 44px. *Mitigation*: The budget recalculation explicitly guarantees `--card-h >= 44px`, and the test directly checks `card.height >= 44 - SLACK_PX`.
- **Click/Drag target obstruction**: In peek mode, if the hand slot clips pointer events or overlapping z-index from the control bar interferes with hand cards or vice versa. *Mitigation*: Component test specifically clicks and drags from the exposed top strip of a hand card, confirming interaction functions cleanly.
- **Duos layout impact**: Duos has a separate rail height and budget (`duos.css:591-593`). *Mitigation*: Duos is left untouched as required; the PR note will mention Duos follow-up.
